_notes: Locked sprite-type specs for PixelKin. The art source of truth is docs/art-style.md; this file operationalises it for generation. Each type fixes a canvas, grid, anchor, and prompt template. Prompt templates use {subject}, {fw}, {fh}, {cols}, {rows}, {canvas_w}, {canvas_h}, {fill_pct}. The shared _style preamble and _originality clause are prepended to every prompt so all types stay consistent and copyright-clean. DO NOT mention the background colour in templates — the skill owns it: for the default OpenAI gpt-image-2 path it prepends a magenta chroma-key preamble and strips the magenta to transparent in post; for the Google path it uses the native transparent route.
_style: Authentic late-1990s / early-2000s handheld pixel art, in the visual register of a Game Boy Color game growing toward Game Boy Advance. STRICT RULES: hard 1-pixel edges, absolutely NO anti-aliasing, no blur, no smooth gradients (a small deliberate dithered pixel gradient is fine). Limited palette of roughly 8-16 colours. A dark outline (deep ink, NOT pure black) around the outer silhouette, lighter internal linework. Consistent light source from the TOP-LEFT. Strong, instantly readable silhouette. Cute, stylised, slightly oversized head and eyes for readability; not realistic, not gritty. Chunky, deliberate square pixels as if drawn pixel-by-pixel on a tiny {fw}x{fh} canvas. No semi-transparent shading. Subject only: no background scenery, no ground, no cast shadow, no frame or border.
_originality: This is original content for PixelKin, a creature-collecting RPG inspired by the genre but a copy of nothing. It must NOT resemble any existing commercial game's creature, character, silhouette, palette signature, logo, font, or UI. Describe by genre and mood only. Make it distinctly original.
_area_style: COHESION: this tile belongs to ONE map area called "{area}" and must read as part of a single unified tile set. Use a shared limited palette of about 10-14 flat colours: {palette}. Keep the SAME pixel density, the SAME top-left light direction, and a matching value range as the rest of the set, so a screen built from these tiles looks like one place and does not visually buzz. Tessellate seamlessly when repeated edge-to-edge; no border, frame, or outline around the tile edge. Light every tile FLATLY and EVENLY (no per-tile vignette or directional shadow) so a field of them never grids.
_block_style: Authentic late-1990s / early-2000s handheld top-down pixel-art TILE ART (Game Boy Color growing toward Game Boy Advance), painted as ONE coherent picture so neighbouring tiles line up and share colours exactly. STRICT RULES: hard 1-pixel edges, absolutely NO anti-aliasing, no blur, no smooth gradients (deliberate dithered pixel gradients are fine). High-CONTRAST limited palette: every material shows a dark shadow tone, a mid body tone AND a bright top-left highlight — never a single flat colour (flatness is the failure to avoid). Consistent light from the TOP-LEFT (lit top/left edges, shadow on bottom/right). Chunky deliberate square pixels on a {tile}-pixel tile grid. No text, no captions, no labels, no drawn grid lines, no frame or border around the whole image. {originality}

terrain-block.label: Autotile terrain block (paint family -> slice)
terrain-block.use_for: A coherent patch of one terrain on its surroundings, containing every edge/corner/inner-corner situation, to slice into an autotile set.
terrain-block.prompt: A top-down TERRAIN PATCH for a retro monster-collecting RPG overworld, on a {cols}x{rows} grid of {tile}px tiles ({canvas_w}x{canvas_h}). Paint an irregular, rounded ISLAND of {subject} sitting on the area's surrounding ground, so the single picture naturally contains, all painted consistently together: large solid CENTRE fill of the terrain; clean straight EDGES where it meets the surroundings on all four sides; rounded OUTER CORNERS; and concave INNER CORNERS where the shape bends back on itself. The terrain reads as gently raised: lit top-left rim, soft shadow on the bottom-right rim. Keep the surrounding ground simple and flat-ish so the terrain's border pixels are the star. Edges and corners MUST align tile-to-tile because they are one image.

scene-mockup.label: Area scene mockup (paint vignette -> harvest)
scene-mockup.use_for: One small top-down vignette of an area to harvest cohesive fill variants + decoration from.
scene-mockup.prompt: A small top-down SCENE VIGNETTE of one place in a retro monster-collecting RPG, on a {cols}x{rows} grid of {tile}px tiles ({canvas_w}x{canvas_h}), as if a screenshot of the game world. Scene: {subject}. Include a few different patches of the area's ground, a path or track crossing it, a little water with its shoreline, a rock or low ledge, and scattered small plants/flowers/pebbles — all in ONE unified palette and light so every tile harvested from it matches. Natural, lived-in arrangement; clear readable shapes at this tiny scale; no characters, no UI, no text.

tile-anim.label: Animated tile frames (paint together -> slice frames)
tile-anim.use_for: The 2-4 frames of one animated tile (water ripple, foam, glowmoss, lamp), painted in a row so they're the same tile with the motion shifted.
tile-anim.prompt: An ANIMATION STRIP of one seamless top-down {subject} tile for a retro monster-collecting RPG, laid out as {cols} frames left-to-right in a {cols}x1 row of {tile}px tiles ({canvas_w}x{canvas_h}). Every frame is the SAME tile — identical palette, layout and edges so it still tessellates — with only the small highlights/ripple shifted a few pixels between frames to read as a gentle loop. Low amplitude, calm motion. No text, no frame numbers, no borders.

tile-sheet.label: Multi-material tile sheet (one call -> slice many tiles)
tile-sheet.use_for: Several DISTINCT materials in one image to slice into separate tiles (cheapest per tile; watch for grid drift).
tile-sheet.prompt: A TILE SHEET for a retro top-down monster-collecting RPG overworld: a strict, perfectly regular grid of EXACTLY {cols} columns by {rows} rows of separate {tile}px world tiles ({canvas_w}x{canvas_h} total). CRITICAL GRID DISCIPLINE: every cell is exactly {tile}x{tile}, the cells abut edge-to-edge with NO gutter, NO margin, NO drawn grid lines, NO labels or numbers, and nothing spans across a cell boundary — each cell is one independent, seamlessly-tileable tile. Read left-to-right then top-to-bottom, the cells are: {subject}. Keep ONE consistent limited palette and a consistent top-left light across the whole sheet so the tiles read as a single matched set. Each ground/water/floor tile must tessellate when its own cell is repeated.

creature-front.label: Creature battle front sprite
creature-front.use_for: The forward-facing battle sprite the player sees of an opponent kin.
creature-front.prompt: A single original creature for a monster-collecting RPG, shown as a battle FRONT sprite: a three-quarter front view, facing the viewer in a calm battle-ready idle pose. Subject: {subject}. The creature should fill about {fill_pct}% of the {fw}x{fh} frame, centred horizontally, body base resting near the lower edge so it 'stands' on the ground line. Whole creature in frame, nothing cropped.

creature-back.label: Creature battle back sprite
creature-back.use_for: The rear-view battle sprite of the player's own kin (back turned to the camera).
creature-back.prompt: The SAME original creature seen from BEHIND for a monster-collecting RPG battle back sprite: a three-quarter view from the rear, back turned to the viewer, battle-ready idle pose. Subject: {subject}. It must read as the SAME species as its front sprite — identical palette, proportions and signature features, just viewed from behind. Fills about {fill_pct}% of the {fw}x{fh} frame, centred horizontally, base near the lower edge.

creature-icon.label: Creature menu icon
creature-icon.use_for: Tiny party/box/menu icon for a kin. Head/silhouette focus, must read at 32px.
creature-icon.prompt: A tiny, simplified menu ICON of an original creature for a monster-collecting RPG, focused on the head and most recognisable silhouette. Subject: {subject}. Drop any fine detail that would vanish at {fw}x{fh}; keep it bold, chunky and instantly readable. Centred in the frame, filling about {fill_pct}%.

creature-overworld.label: Creature overworld mini-sprite
creature-overworld.use_for: A kin roaming the overworld. Very simple, single idle frame by default.
creature-overworld.prompt: A very simple overworld mini-sprite of an original creature for a monster-collecting RPG, in a gentle top-down-leaning view, single idle pose. Subject: {subject}. Keep it minimal and charming — readable at {fw}x{fh}, the same species as its battle sprite but simplified. Centred horizontally, feet near the lower edge, filling about {fill_pct}% of the frame.

creature-portrait.label: Creature portrait
creature-portrait.use_for: Larger profile / dex art for a kin. Richer than the battle sprite, same character.
creature-portrait.prompt: A portrait / dex illustration of an original creature for a monster-collecting RPG: a characterful three-quarter front bust or full pose with a touch more colour and detail than the small battle sprite, but the SAME character, palette and personality. Subject: {subject}. Centred in the {fw}x{fh} frame, filling about {fill_pct}%.

human-overworld.label: Human / NPC overworld walk sheet
human-overworld.use_for: A walking character sheet for towns and routes: 4 columns x 4 rows, 32px frames (a real walk cycle, not a 2-frame shuffle).
human-overworld.prompt: An original human character walking sprite SHEET for a retro monster-collecting RPG, laid out as a strict grid of {cols} columns by {rows} rows of {fw}x{fh} frames ({canvas_w}x{canvas_h} total). Rows are facing directions top to bottom: row 1 facing DOWN, row 2 facing LEFT, row 3 facing RIGHT, row 4 facing UP. CRUCIAL — each row is drawn from the VIEWPOINT that matches its direction, and the four rows must be unmistakably different views of the character, NOT the same front pose repeated: the DOWN row faces the viewer (we see the FULL FACE, both eyes, the front of the body); the LEFT row is seen from the character's LEFT — the character faces the LEFT edge of the frame in side / three-quarter profile, nose and body turned left, only the left side of the face and ONE eye visible; the RIGHT row is the exact MIRROR of the left row, facing the RIGHT edge; the UP row is seen FROM BEHIND — we see the BACK of the head and shoulders (hair and the back of the jacket only), with NO face and NO eyes visible at all. Never draw a forward-facing face in the LEFT, RIGHT or UP rows — in the UP row the back of the head must be visible in EVERY column including the walk frames. Columns are a WALK CYCLE left to right: column 1 IDLE (standing, weight even, both feet planted); column 2 CONTACT-LEFT (left foot planted forward, right leg trailing back, arms swung in opposition); column 3 PASSING (both legs together under the body mid-stride, and the WHOLE body raised by 1 pixel so the head bobs); column 4 CONTACT-RIGHT (the mirror of column 2 — right foot forward, left trailing). Within a row, the facing and viewpoint stay IDENTICAL across all four columns — only the legs, arms and the 1px passing lift change from column to column. Character: {subject}. The two contact poses (cols 2 and 4) must be CLEARLY different from each other — visible leg crossover and opposite arm swing — or the walk reads as a shuffle. Keep head height, proportions and palette identical in every frame. Feet sit on the SAME baseline in the idle and both contact frames; the passing frame is 1px higher. Centred horizontally, about 20-24px wide inside each 32px frame. Even spacing, one pose isolated per cell.

human-actions.label: Human action / pose sheet (optional, layer 3)
human-actions.use_for: Optional bespoke event poses for a character (mainly the player): raise-lamp/relight, lamp-toss/catch, Lantern-Gift cast, sit, hurt. Front-facing (toward camera). Pairs with the base human-overworld walk sheet of the SAME character; pass that sheet as --reference so the body matches.
human-actions.prompt: An original wordless human-character pose sheet for a retro monster-collecting RPG. ABSOLUTE RULE, MOST IMPORTANT: this image contains ZERO text — no words, no labels, no captions, no titles, no letters, no numbers, no writing of any kind in any cell. Draw ONLY the character figure in each cell, nothing written. Layout: a strict grid of {cols} columns by {rows} rows of {fw}x{fh} frames ({canvas_w}x{canvas_h} total), read left-to-right then top-to-bottom. Every cell shows the SAME character from the front (facing the viewer), standing on the same baseline with identical head height, proportions and palette — only the arms, body and the small handheld lantern they carry change between cells. Character: {subject}. The eight cells, in order, are these poses: first, beginning to lift the little lantern with the arm bent at the chest; second, the lantern held high overhead at arm's length and glowing, head tilted up; third, body coiled with the lantern drawn back beside the head ready to throw; fourth, the arm thrown forward and fully extended as the lantern just leaves the hand; fifth, both hands bringing the lantern up in front of the chest; sixth, the lantern thrust forward at arm's length casting light ahead; seventh, sitting on the ground with knees up, relaxed; eighth, flinching backward with one arm raised and knees bent in recoil. Centred horizontally, feet on the same baseline in the standing cells, about 20-24px wide inside each {fw}px frame, one clear pose isolated per cell with even spacing. Remember: absolutely no text or lettering anywhere.
human-actions._engine_layout: Actor.HUMAN_ACTION_FRAMES: raiseLamp=[0,1], toss=[2,3], gift=[4,5], sit=[6], hurt=[7] (row-major).

human-pose.label: Single human action pose (assemble into an action sheet)
human-pose.use_for: ONE front-facing character pose on a 32x32 frame — the ROBUST way to build a human-actions sheet (image models are weak at multi-pose grids). Generate each pose with the character's walk sheet as --reference, then assemble the 4x2 sheet with assemble_action_sheet.py.
human-pose.prompt: A single original human character POSE sprite for a retro monster-collecting RPG: ONE figure only, seen from the FRONT (facing the viewer), centred horizontally with the feet near the lower edge so it stands on the ground line. Character and pose: {subject}. Fills about {fill_pct}% of the {fw}x{fh} frame, whole figure in frame, nothing cropped. CRITICAL: exactly ONE single figure — not a row, not a grid, not multiple copies — and absolutely NO text, NO labels, NO words, NO numbers anywhere.

emote.label: Shared overworld emote / status bubble sheet (layer 2, reusable by ALL characters)
emote.use_for: One shared sheet of floating reaction bubbles popped above any character's head during cutscenes/events (surprise, question, heart, etc.). Generate ONCE; reused across every character — do not bake emotes into per-character sheets.
emote.prompt: A sheet of original floating EMOTE / status BUBBLES for a retro monster-collecting RPG, the little symbols that pop above a character's head in a cutscene. Strict grid of {cols} columns by {rows} rows of {fw}x{fh} frames ({canvas_w}x{canvas_h} total), read left-to-right then top-to-bottom. Each cell holds ONE small rounded speech-bubble with a bold symbol inside it, centred in the cell, NO character or scenery — the bubble only, with its little tail pointing down. The eight bubbles are, in order: (1) a bold EXCLAMATION mark '!' (surprise/alert); (2) a QUESTION mark '?' (confusion); (3) a HEART (affection); (4) an ELLIPSIS of three dots '...' (speechless/thinking); (5) a SWEAT-DROP (awkward/nervous); (6) a sleepy double-Z 'Zz' (sleeping/bored); (7) a MUSIC NOTE (happy/humming); (8) an ANGER cross-pop / vein mark (annoyed). Bright, chunky, instantly readable at tiny size, consistent top-left light, dark non-black outline. One bubble per cell, even spacing.
emote._engine_layout: Actor.EMOTE_FRAMES: alert=0, question=1, heart=2, ellipsis=3, sweat=4, sleep=5, music=6, anger=7 (row-major).

effect.label: Battle effect frame sheet
effect.use_for: A reusable battle effect animation (spark, slash, burst, splash) as a frame grid.
effect.prompt: An original battle EFFECT animation sheet for a retro monster-collecting RPG, laid out as a strict grid of {cols} columns by {rows} rows of {fw}x{fh} frames ({canvas_w}x{canvas_h} total), read left-to-right then top-to-bottom as the animation progresses from start to dissipation. Effect: {subject}. Each frame is one moment of the animation, centred in its cell. Bright, punchy, chunky pixel shapes; no creature or character in the frames — the effect only. Even spacing, one frame per cell.

tile.label: World tile
tile.use_for: A single 16x16 tileable world tile (grass, path, water edge, etc.).
tile.prompt: A single original {fw}x{fh} world TILE for a retro top-down monster-collecting RPG overworld, designed to tessellate seamlessly when repeated edge-to-edge on a grid. Tile: {subject}. Fill the whole {fw}x{fh} frame to the edges (no margin, no outline around the tile border). Keep interior detail low and evenly distributed so a field of these tiles does not visually buzz or show an obvious repeat. Light the surface FLATLY and EVENLY across the entire tile — no vignette, no corner or edge shadows, no darkening toward the borders, no single baked-in light source — otherwise repeated tiles form a visible grid. BEST RESULTS: generate this as a large continuous swatch and downscale the whole image (or slice an interior cell of a block), never as one bordered tile.

tile-ground.label: Ground fill tile
tile-ground.use_for: A seamless interior ground-fill tile for an area set (grass, dirt, sand, stone floor).
tile-ground.prompt: A single original {fw}x{fh} GROUND-FILL world tile for a retro top-down monster-collecting RPG, the base surface a player walks on across a whole field. Surface: {subject}. Fill the frame edge-to-edge with low, even interior detail so a large field of these tiles reads as one smooth surface with no obvious seam or repeating hotspot. Light the surface FLATLY and EVENLY across the entire tile — no vignette, no corner or edge shadows, no darkening toward the borders, no single baked-in light source — otherwise repeated tiles form a visible grid. BEST RESULTS: generate this as a large continuous swatch and downscale the whole image (or slice an interior cell of a block), never as one bordered tile.

tile-path.label: Path / road tile
tile-path.use_for: A seamless path or road tile that tessellates into a walkway through ground tiles.
tile-path.prompt: A single original {fw}x{fh} PATH tile for a retro top-down monster-collecting RPG: the trodden walkway surface. Path: {subject}. Fill the frame edge-to-edge so straight runs of the tile form a continuous path; keep edges neutral so it abuts the area's ground tile cleanly. Low, even detail, no border line around the tile. Light the surface FLATLY and EVENLY across the entire tile — no vignette, no corner or edge shadows, no darkening toward the borders, no single baked-in light source — otherwise repeated tiles form a visible grid. BEST RESULTS: generate this as a large continuous swatch and downscale the whole image (or slice an interior cell of a block), never as one bordered tile.

tile-water.label: Open water tile
tile-water.use_for: A seamless open-water tile (sea, lake, river body).
tile-water.prompt: A single original {fw}x{fh} open-WATER tile for a retro top-down monster-collecting RPG. Water: {subject}. Fill the frame edge-to-edge with a gently rippled surface that tessellates so a large body of water reads as continuous, no obvious repeat. Low, even detail; no shoreline or border in this tile (that is the separate water-edge tile). Light the surface FLATLY and EVENLY across the entire tile — no vignette, no corner or edge shadows, no darkening toward the borders, no single baked-in light source — otherwise repeated tiles form a visible grid. BEST RESULTS: generate this as a large continuous swatch and downscale the whole image (or slice an interior cell of a block), never as one bordered tile.

tile-water-edge.label: Water/land edge tile
tile-water-edge.use_for: The transition tile where water meets land; pairs with the set's water and ground tiles.
tile-water-edge.prompt: A single original {fw}x{fh} WATER-EDGE transition tile for a retro top-down monster-collecting RPG: the boundary where water meets land, with water along one side and shoreline/ground along the other. Edge: {subject}. The water side must tessellate with the set's plain water tile and the land side with the set's ground tile, so it slots between them with no seam. Fill the frame edge-to-edge, no border line. Keep lighting FLAT and EVEN along the axis this tile repeats on (no vignette, no end-darkening) so it shows no seam when tiled; only the perpendicular transition side carries gradient. BEST RESULTS: paint the transition as a long strip and slice a clean interior cross-section, not one bordered tile.

tile-cliff.label: Cliff / ledge face tile
tile-cliff.use_for: A vertical cliff or ledge face tile (the wall of a height change).
tile-cliff.prompt: A single original {fw}x{fh} CLIFF-FACE tile for a retro top-down monster-collecting RPG: the vertical rock/earth face of a ledge or height drop, tiling horizontally along a cliff and vertically down a tall face. Face: {subject}. Fill the frame edge-to-edge; keep it readable as a solid impassable wall. Low, even detail, no border line. Light the surface FLATLY and EVENLY across the entire tile — no vignette, no corner or edge shadows, no darkening toward the borders, no single baked-in light source — otherwise repeated tiles form a visible grid. BEST RESULTS: generate this as a large continuous swatch and downscale the whole image (or slice an interior cell of a block), never as one bordered tile.

tile-cliff-edge.label: Cliff top-edge tile
tile-cliff-edge.use_for: The top lip of a cliff where the upper ground meets the cliff face; pairs with cliff + ground.
tile-cliff-edge.prompt: A single original {fw}x{fh} CLIFF-TOP-EDGE tile for a retro top-down monster-collecting RPG: the lip where upper ground meets the start of a cliff face below. Edge: {subject}. The top must tessellate with the set's ground tile and the bottom with the set's cliff-face tile, so it slots between them. Fill the frame edge-to-edge, no border line. Keep lighting FLAT and EVEN along the axis this tile repeats on (no vignette, no end-darkening) so it shows no seam when tiled; only the perpendicular transition side carries gradient. BEST RESULTS: paint the transition as a long strip and slice a clean interior cross-section, not one bordered tile.

tile-roof.prompt: A single original {fw}x{fh} building-ROOF tile for a retro top-down monster-collecting RPG, tiling across the top of a structure. Roof: {subject}. Fill the frame edge-to-edge so a roof area reads as continuous; consistent top-left light. Low, even detail, no border line.

Fill the frame edge-to-edge so walls tile horizontally; consistent top-left light. Low, even detail, no border line. Light the surface FLATLY and EVENLY across the entire tile — no vignette, no corner or edge shadows, no darkening toward the borders, no single baked-in light source — otherwise repeated tiles form a visible grid. Fill the frame edge-to-edge with low, even grainy detail so a beach of these tiles reads as one continuous surface with no obvious seam or repeat. tile-floor.prompt: A single original {fw}x{fh} FLOOR fill tile for a retro top-down monster-collecting RPG: a paved plaza or board/wood floor a player walks on. Surface: {subject}. Fill the frame edge-to-edge; if it has planks or paving, align them so the tile tessellates into a continuous regular floor with no broken seam. Low, even detail, no border line. tile-door.label: Door tile
tile-door.use_for: A door tile set into a wall (an entrance the player faces); fills its frame, abuts the wall tile.

tile-fence.prompt: A single original {fw}x{fh} FENCE tile for a retro top-down monster-collecting RPG: a low wooden fence or railing seen from the front, the rail running horizontally so a row of these tiles forms one continuous fence. Fence: {subject}. The rail sits in the lower-middle of the tile with transparent space above it; the posts align so the tile repeats horizontally with no break. Consistent top-left light, dark non-black outline.

tile-decor.label: Decoration tile
tile-decor.use_for: A small standalone decoration that sits on a deco layer over ground (flower, sign, crate, lamp). Keeps transparency around it.
tile-decor.prompt: A single small original {fw}x{fh} DECORATION object for a retro top-down monster-collecting RPG overworld, sitting alone so it can be placed over a ground tile (transparent around the object, NOT a full edge-to-edge surface). Object: {subject}. Centred in the frame, chunky and readable at {fw}x{fh}, consistent top-left light, dark non-black outline.
